title: Kani shawl weaving by talim code
summary: In the Kashmir valley, weavers build a fine goat-wool shawl on a frame loom with dozens of small wooden bobbins, one for each patch of colour. A coded chart called talim is read aloud row by row, and the pattern grows in the cloth itself.
howToPlay: Look at the chart card: it shows the motif and thread colour wanted in each square.
Pick a thread colour from the spools, then a motif.
Touch a square to weave it. The shawl is a mirror of itself left to right, so the partner square is woven too.
Press Check to compare your cloth with the chart and earn up to three stars.
rules: The shawl pattern is symmetric left to right: every stitch you place appears on its mirror square.
Placing the same motif and colour again on a square removes it.
One colour patch belongs to one bobbin, so each square must match the colour of the chart exactly.
Score is the share of squares that match the chart; 98 percent or more earns three stars, 85 percent two, 60 percent one.
heritageNote: Kani weaving comes from Kanihama and nearby villages in Kashmir, India, where weavers, chart writers and dyers each hold a part of the craft. A single shawl can take many months to finish.
credits: Chart designs are our own simplified patterns after boteh, jaal and leaf borders of the tradition.
